bihar_raw_news.title: Samrat Choudhary warns of action within 24 hours against those targeting women in Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo: Samrat Choudhary's X account) India 6th October 2026 Patna, October 6 (IANS) Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday visited Sasaram in Rohtas district and addressed a 'Yuva Samvad' programme at Jamuhar, where he spoke about women's safety, law and order and the development of the state. Addressing the gathering, Choudhary said that given the prevailing security environment in the state, anyone who dares to harm or molest women will face action within 24 hours. He said he was making this commitment to the women of Bihar in his capacity as the state's leader. Referring to five videos of incidents that had surfaced from different parts of Bihar, Chief Minister Choudhary said immediate action had been taken in the cases. He also added that millions of women are now stepping out of their homes to work, attributing the change to the governance of the NDA. Targeting the Opposition, the Chief Minister said that some people view political power as an opportunity for personal gain, whereas the NDA and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) consider power a means to serve the people. Praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chief Minister Choudhary said that despite being in power for 25 consecutive years, PM Modi had remained committed to serving the public and continued to uphold that approach. He contrasted the present situation in Bihar with the period before 2005, recalling that areas of Rohtas and Kaimur had once been affected by the activities of dacoits and that people were fearful of travelling from Kaimur towards Ara. He said the situation had changed significantly and reiterated that anyone who harms a woman in Bihar would face arrest within 24 hours. The event was attended by MP BD Singh, former MP Gopal Narayan Singh, MLA Trivikram Narayan Singh and BJP leader Bhikhubhai Dalsania. During his Rohtas visit, CM Choudhary inaugurated the Sasaram Bypass and inspected the Beda Flyover. The 9.2-km Beda-Mokar bypass is a part of the Bihar government's infrastructure push in the district. He also inspected a pond renovated under the 'Kayakalp Abhiyan' and reviewed ongoing development works in the area. Earlier, CM Choudhary addressed a gathering after inaugurating an astronomy laboratory at the PM SHRI Kendriya Vidyalaya in Karup Panchayat under Shivsagar block. He also participated in the 'Seva Setu Abhiyan' support camp and reviewed various government schemes and development initiatives. The Chief Minister also interacted with youth at the Narayan Medical College in Sasaram as part of his outreach programme.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 157 Union Cabinet approves Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority
national_raw_news.content: Union Cabinet has approved the setting up of the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA). Briefing the media in New Delhi today after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that this will strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment across the transportation and logistics sector. He said, it will serve as the apex body for integrated transport and logstic planning in the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, as the country’s GDP is growing at a rate of around 7 to 8 percent, the demand for logistics is also increasing continuously. The Minister said that several highways, railway lines, waterways, airports and new ports are being developed across the country to meet this growing demand. The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority will prepare a long-term National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of ten years. With the expansion of the transport and logistics networks, ITLA will support long-term integrated planning and post-implementation impact assessment of infrastructure projects. It will complement existing initiatives such as the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and the National Logistics Policy. ITLA will undertake a range of responsibilities covering integrated planning, project appraisal, monitoring, data analytics, logistics policy, capacity building and research. The authority will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more. It will cover roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics. It will also monitor transport and infrastructure projects costing above 5 hundred crore rupees, providing a coordinated mechanism for issue resolution. ITLA will promote research and innovations in transport and logistics sectors. Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in realising India’s Vision 2047 by strengthening multimodal connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness. Union Cabinet has also approved the establishment of ten thousand crore rupees Small and Medium Enterprises Growth fund for equity investments in Small and Medium Enterprises. Mr Vaishnav said, the fund will provide long term equity capital to high potential Small and Medium Enterprises with demonstrated business viability and ability to scale. The Minister said that the majority of funds allocation will go towards manufacturing focused Small and Medium Enterprises. It will also support enterprises across services, technology, innovation driven sectors and strategic value chain.
